answer: Each agent must occupy exactly one surveyed monument on a hard-capped geodetic grid that runs from an inland summit down to a coastal reef. Enrollment fuses the monument's measured baseline and a tagged cedar witness post to a single signing key. Random audits require a fresh signed total-station reading that peers recompute against the published control network; a second key on the same monument forfeits the occupancy bond. Every alias therefore needs its own scarce monument plus a new field survey, a linear capital and logistics cost that cloned software cannot share.
